message: Bravo! On the evasion of "inequality," you might play around with the word "winner." Is it inequality when one football team wins the Superbowl, and the others are ranked below it in the League Standings. I think the myth is that we all have an equal or fair chance to win, but that only the winners get the trophies. Thus we can feel contempt for the losers, who die in the gutters. They earned themselves that dubious privilege. They are losers and get what they deserve. Likewise we idolize winners who come up from nothing, validating our faith that the system rewards hard work and ability. "Meritocracy," "Social Darwinism." The most potent argument might be that the game is rigged in favor of those who start with certain advantages -- that would be real class system, as opposed to a meritocracy with differential but fair outcomes.
